reasons: Reads cast the database row to a loose type, so a wrong field name would fail quietly.

sections.name: File setup, ResearchSourceInput
sections.title: Imports and source record shape
sections.what: Loads the database tools and defines the fields a research source must provide.
sections.why: The comment states research must not silently edit project facts.
sections.watch_out: The URL and quote fields are required, and blank values pass through without a check.

sections.name: researchSourceId
sections.title: Stable source ID
sections.what: Makes an ID from the URL, quote, capture time and optional claim, so the same capture always gets the same ID.
sections.why: The comment states older citations must keep their date and identity.
sections.watch_out: Changing the capture time or any input creates a new ID, so older links no longer match.

sections.name: registerResearchSource
sections.title: Saving a source
sections.what: Saves a source record if it is new, then returns it with its ID. Saving the same source again changes nothing.
sections.why: The SQL states insert, and ignore if the ID already exists.
sections.watch_out: Only the first saved copy is kept. Later changes to the same ID are ignored.

sections.name: getResearchEvidence
sections.title: Reading a source back
sections.what: Looks up a saved source by ID and turns it into the evidence format the rest of the app uses.
sections.why: Likely reason: other code expects the evidence shape.
sections.watch_out: Missing fields become empty text or a default field path, which can hide missing data.

sections.name: mergeResearchSourceKeys
sections.title: Adding source tags
sections.what: Adds extra key-value tags to an existing saved source.
sections.why: Likely reason: adds labels without changing the main record.
sections.watch_out: If the ID does not exist, nothing is changed and no error is raised.

summary: Stores where each research quote came from and gives it a stable ID, while keeping that record separate from the project's facts.
purpose: Keep a citation for every research quote so it can be traced later.
why: The header states that research never silently edits project facts, so sources live in their own record.
how: Builds an ID from the URL, quote, capture time, and optional claim. Saves the record if the ID is new. Reads a record back in the evidence format. Adds extra key tags to an existing record.
inputs: A source record with URL, title, quote, publisher, check date, and optional claim, project, and field names.
outputs: A stored record with its ID, or an evidence object read back by ID.
risks: The same source captured on a different date gets a different ID, which can orphan older links. Deleting rows would break citations. Reads are loosely typed.
debug: Look up the research_sources row by ID. If a lookup returns undefined, the ID may have changed because the capture date changed. Compare checkedAt values.
